$comment: Generated by scripts/build_indicator_contract.py from gg_indicators/source/Indicators.xlsx + gg_indicators/settings/*.json - do not hand-edit.
sheet_weights_note: The sheet's two weight columns are deliberately empty; weights live in versioned weight sets (gg_indicators/settings/weight_sets/).
axis_rule: contains CONTEXT -> CONTEXT; else contains BOTH -> BOTH; else contains uppercase READINESS -> READINESS; else NEED (case sensitive on purpose)

variables.label: Management Age
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn executive profiles, company leadership page, Handelsregister officer records, press bios

sources: AIDA officers export -> company_people (age)
Registro Imprese / visura camerale (cariche)

variables.proxy: Average age of the executive team (CEO, CFO, COO, board), from public bios or officer records
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] A younger executive team tends to be less anchored to legacy habits and faster to adopt new practices, echoing the 'young generation ready to revolutionize the business model' pattern already used in VIENNA to flag succession-driven openness.
variables.comment: Correlation, not causation: some young leaders are more conservative than their predecessors. Use jointly with 'New Generation of Management' rather than alone.

variables.label: Management National diversity
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn, company leadership page, press bios

sources: AIDA officers export -> company_people (nationality)
Registro Imprese / visura camerale

variables.proxy: Nationality mix of the executive team and board, from public bios/LinkedIn
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Executives with international backgrounds are more likely to have been exposed to open-innovation practices abroad and less anchored to purely domestic norms.
variables.comment: Weak signal alone; most useful combined with the International Sales Volume and Years of International Activity rows.

variables.label: Management cultural diversity
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn, bios, education history

sources: TO_MAP: no Italian registry field; LinkedIn / company leadership page bios

variables.proxy: Cultural/educational background mix of the executive team, inferred from bios and education history across countries
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] A management team drawing on varied cultural reference points tends to score higher on openness to unfamiliar ideas, similar to nationality diversity.
variables.comment: Overlaps heavily with Management National Diversity, treat as a secondary confirmation signal rather than an independent one to avoid double-counting in a composite score.

variables.label: Management gender diversity
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn, company leadership page, Handelsregister officer listing

sources: AIDA officers export -> company_people (gender)
Registro Imprese / visura camerale

variables.proxy: % of women in the executive team and on the supervisory board
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] More gender-balanced leadership teams are associated in the management literature with broader information search and less groupthink, a weak positive proxy for openness.
variables.comment: Evidence in the literature is mixed with small effect sizes; weight lower than succession or education signals in any composite score.

variables.label: Management level of education
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn education history, university alumni announcements, press bios

sources: TO_MAP: not in AIDA or the Registro Imprese; LinkedIn education history only

variables.proxy: Share of the executive team holding a university degree or higher (Master's / MBA / PhD)
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Higher formal education correlates with greater comfort engaging with a structured, metrics-driven pilot framework like GG's, and faster uptake of unfamiliar analytical tools.
variables.comment: Confidence: medium. Education level is easy to source for executives but rarely disclosed for the wider workforce, so treat this specifically as a leadership-team variable.

variables.label: Management diversity of education
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn education history

sources: TO_MAP: LinkedIn education history only

variables.proxy: Range of academic disciplines represented across the executive team (engineering, business, law, sciences, etc.)
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Cross-disciplinary leadership is more likely to recognize an unfamiliar external idea as relevant rather than dismiss it as outside its frame of reference.
variables.comment: Confidence: medium, and best read together with row 6 rather than as an independent signal.

variables.label: New Generation of management

status_mapping.note: Row 8 [BOTH]: a recent handover is a NEED signal and a READINESS signal; one observation feeds both axes through its own mapping.

variables.source_text_sheet: Handelsregister officer change filings, press releases announcing new CEO/MD, company 'our story' page

sources: AIDA officers export -> company_people (age + appointment dates) via sync_succession_signal
Registro Imprese / visura camerale (variazioni cariche)

variables.proxy: Family surname appearance in management
variables.indicator_text: [BOTH] A recent generational handover is both a NEED signal (incoming leadership typically wants to establish its own track record and reposition the business) and a READINESS signal (a newly installed generation is usually the most open to revising the business model, matching the succession pattern already flagged in VIENNA).
variables.comment: The strongest single trigger-event variable in this table. Pair with Management Age for confirmation; treat a handover under 2 years old as a priority outreach signal.

variables.label: Turnover of management
variables.source_text_sheet: Handelsregister officer change filings, press releases

sources: AIDA officers export -> company_people (appointment / resignation dates)
Registro Imprese / visura camerale (variazioni cariche)

variables.proxy: Number of C-suite/MD changes in the past 3 years
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Frequent leadership turnover often coincides with a company actively searching for a new strategic direction, a NEED signal, though it carries the execution risk already noted in the existing comment.
variables.comment: Could be a liability: company needs to find its way, but might not have the time

variables.label: External collaboration
variables.source_text_sheet: Press releases, university/accelerator case studies, company 'partners' page, patent co-assignments

sources: TO_MAP: press / university case studies; no Italian registry

variables.proxy: Documented past partnerships with startups, universities, accelerators, or corporate venturing programs
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Prior participation in any external collaboration is the strongest behavioral proof of readiness available: it is revealed preference, not stated intent, and directly de-risks GG's pitch since the company has already cleared its internal approval hurdle once before.
variables.comment: Weight more heavily than any self-reported openness variable, since it reflects observed behavior rather than a survey response.

variables.label: Interdepartmental collaboration
variables.source_text_sheet: First-contact questionnaire (primary data), job postings mentioning cross-functional work, org chart if published

sources: First-contact questionnaire (primary data); no registry

variables.proxy: Not directly observable pre-contact in most cases; approximated via org-chart flatness or job postings mentioning 'cross-functional teams'
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Low silo-ing correlates with faster internal alignment to actually launch and staff a time-boxed pilot without a lengthy internal negotiation.
variables.comment: Genuinely hard to source externally; best captured through a short first-contact questionnaire during the Diagnosi/scoping call rather than desk research.

variables.label: Verticality in the structure
variables.source_text_sheet: First-contact questionnaire, org chart if published, headcount as a rough proxy (smaller firms tend to be flatter)

sources: First-contact questionnaire; org chart if published

variables.proxy: Number of management layers between CEO and frontline staff, or self-reported at first contact
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Flatter hierarchies shorten the pilot approval chain, directly reducing the 'commitment gap / long complex sale' risk already flagged for SKEPTIC-level companies in VIENNA.
variables.comment: Same sourcing limitation as the row above; best confirmed at first contact rather than assumed from desk research.

variables.label: Employee turnover
variables.source_text_sheet: LinkedIn tenure distribution, Kununu/Glassdoor reviews, Bundesagentur für Arbeit regional turnover statistics as benchmark

sources: TO_MAP: LinkedIn tenure distribution, Indeed/Glassdoor company reviews (Italy); no registry series

variables.proxy: Staff attrition rate, estimated via LinkedIn tenure distribution or Kununu/Glassdoor review mentions
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Low turnover signals a stable operating base able to sustain a structured pilot through to completion. Flag the dual reading: very low turnover can also mean entrenched routines and resistance to change, so treat this as a necessary-but-not-sufficient enabler rather than a positive openness signal on its own.
variables.comment: Cross-reference against Kununu/Glassdoor sentiment (see new row below) before scoring, since low turnover with poor reviews likely means people are staying out of necessity, not satisfaction.

variables.label: Number of Employees
variables.source_text_sheet: Handelsregister, company website, LinkedIn company page, Bundesanzeiger filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Dipendenti' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)
Registro Imprese / INPS-based addetti where available (TO_MAP)

variables.proxy: Headcount, from Handelsregister/company register filings or LinkedIn company page
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Primarily a segment-fit filter rather than a need/openness signal: it operationalizes your own Mittelstand-vs-SME distinction, large enough to have structured budget and some innovation appetite, small enough to still move fast.
variables.comment: Set explicit lower/upper headcount bounds once Stage 1 pilot data shows what actually worked; this variable should anchor your segment cutoff.
differences: axis: sheet READINESS vs catalog CONTEXT
role: sheet Scored but catalog treats it as context (unscored)

variables.label: Average Salary
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings (Personalaufwand line), Kununu/Glassdoor salary estimates

sources: AIDA export header 'Totale costi del personale' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC) divided by AIDA export header 'Dipendenti' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Average personnel cost per employee (Personalaufwand ÷ headcount), from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Above-average pay suggests the company can attract and retain more skilled staff, a proxy for the internal capacity needed to actually run and absorb a pilot's findings.
variables.comment: Benchmark against sector-average personnel cost per employee rather than an absolute threshold, since 'Medium-High' varies a lot by industry.
differences: automation_tier: sheet mode 'Web or job board scrape' -> T2 vs catalog T1

variables.label: Skilled Labour
variables.source_text_sheet: Job postings (Stepstone, Indeed), LinkedIn employee skill/role data

sources: TO_MAP: Italian job boards (InfoJobs, Indeed Italia, LinkedIn), no registry field

variables.proxy: Share of roles requiring a technical/university qualification, from job postings and LinkedIn skill tags
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] A more technically skilled workforce lowers the onboarding cost of a new tool or process, directly reducing pilot execution risk.
variables.comment: Overlaps with Average Salary; the two together are a stronger signal than either alone.

variables.label: Volume of online sales
variables.source_text_sheet: Similarweb/website traffic estimate, annual report management commentary, industry benchmark reports

sources: TO_MAP: Similarweb traffic estimate; bilancio notes rarely split online sales

variables.proxy: Estimated e-commerce revenue share, from website/checkout presence or annual report management commentary
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Low online sales volume relative to industry peers is a direct, quantifiable innovation gap, precisely the kind of unmet need a digital-enablement pilot can target.
variables.comment: Hard to estimate precisely without direct disclosure; treat any figure derived from traffic tools as directional, not exact.

variables.label: Online market presence
variables.source_text_sheet: Company website audit, BuiltWith/Wayback Machine, social media presence check

sources: Company website audit, Wayback Machine (company_website_crawler / digital_maturity_crawler)

variables.proxy: Presence and quality of e-commerce site, social media activity, SEO visibility
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] An underdeveloped online presence is one of the most visible, easily verified NEED signals available before any direct contact, and one of the easiest pilot categories to scope (digital storefront, marketing automation, etc.).
variables.comment: Fastest variable to check pre-contact, worth using as an early-stage filter before investing research time in the harder-to-source financial variables.

variables.label: Number of physical stores

applicability.rationale: No stores for a pure B2B firm.

variables.source_text_sheet: Company website store locator, press releases, historical Google Maps listings

sources: Company website store locator; Registro Imprese unita locali (TO_MAP: field)

variables.proxy: Store count over time, from company website store locator or press releases
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A shrinking physical footprint without a compensating digital channel signals an unaddressed transition problem, exactly the kind of structural need GG's channel-innovation pilots exist to solve.
variables.comment: If the company is pure B2B with no retail footprint, this variable does not apply; treat as null rather than 'zero = need'.

variables.label: Geographic distribution of stores

applicability.rationale: No stores for a pure B2B firm.

variables.source_text_sheet: Company website, Handelsregister branch (Zweigniederlassung) filings

sources: Company website store locator; Registro Imprese unita locali (TO_MAP: field)

variables.proxy: Number of distinct regions/postal areas served, from store locator or delivery-area disclosure
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A geographically concentrated footprint with no digital expansion into other regions represents unrealized growth GG could help unlock via new channels.
variables.comment: Same B2B applicability caveat as the row above.
differences: automation_tier: sheet mode 'Registry or filing' -> T1 vs catalog T2

variables.label: International Sales volume
variables.source_text_sheet: Annual report segment notes, IHK (Chamber of Commerce) export statistics, Germany Trade & Invest data

sources: Bilancio / nota integrativa geographic split (TO_MAP: not a standard AIDA column); Eurostat export exposure is only a sector macro proxy

variables.proxy: Export revenue share, from annual report segment notes if disclosed, or Chamber of Commerce export data
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Stagnant international sales despite an otherwise viable product is a classic unrealized-opportunity signal, and a strong one specifically for GG's German-Italian bridge extension.
variables.comment: Where segment notes are not disclosed, a rough proxy is whether the company website exists in more than one language.

variables.label: Years of international activity
variables.source_text_sheet: Handelsregister foreign branch filings, company 'our history' page, trade press

sources: TO_MAP: Camera di Commercio / ICE directories, company 'our history' page

variables.proxy: Year of first recorded export activity or first foreign subsidiary/branch registration
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Limited international experience means the company likely lacks internal playbooks for cross-border expansion, a NEED signal, but it also flags lower READINESS to execute a cross-border pilot without hands-on support.
variables.comment: Treat as a NEED signal on the product/market axis, and a readiness caveat on execution capacity; don't double-count it as purely positive.
differences: automation_tier: sheet mode 'Manual desk research' -> T2 vs catalog T1

variables.label: Product demand
variables.source_text_sheet: Industry classification/category norms, review-aggregator sentiment (Google/Trustpilot), press coverage of pricing behavior

sources: TO_MAP: sector norms; no registry

variables.proxy: Price elasticity inferred from category (discretionary vs. staple good) and any available sales-price correlation data
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] As already noted in the VIENNA source notes, companies with elastic demand have a stronger built-in incentive to keep customers happy, which translates into higher motivation to adopt a pilot that improves the customer experience.
variables.comment: A motivation proxy, not a capability one; still requires the other readiness variables to be present.

variables.label: Product differentiation
variables.source_text_sheet: Marketplace/competitor listings, industry trade reports, product catalogs

sources: TO_MAP: marketplace / catalog comparison (product_catalog_crawler)

variables.proxy: Number of comparable competing products at similar price points, from marketplace listings or industry reports
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A commoditized, undifferentiated product is under constant margin pressure and has the clearest need for an innovation-driven differentiation strategy.
variables.comment: Best assessed together with Innovativeness of Product and Quality of Product rather than in isolation.

variables.label: Product portfolio diversity
variables.source_text_sheet: Company catalog/website, industry association member directories

sources: Company catalog / website (product_catalog_crawler)

variables.proxy: Number of distinct product lines or SKUs disclosed on the company website/catalog
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A narrow product portfolio concentrates revenue risk in a small number of lines, strengthening the case for innovation-driven diversification.
variables.comment: A very narrow portfolio in a niche B2B category is not automatically a red flag, check whether the niche itself is stable or shrinking before scoring this as NEED.

variables.label: Rarity of raw materials
variables.source_text_sheet: Industry/commodity reports, annual report risk disclosures, procurement trade press

sources: TO_MAP: commodity reports, bilancio risk disclosure

variables.proxy: Number of alternative suppliers available for the primary input, from procurement/industry reports
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Dependence on a scarce input is a direct supply-risk pressure point that process or material-substitution innovation can address.
variables.comment: Applies mainly to manufacturing and materials-intensive sectors; treat as not applicable for services businesses.

variables.label: Cost of raw materials
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings, industry cost benchmark reports

sources: AIDA export header 'Materie prime e consumo' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Input cost as % of COGS, from annual report notes if disclosed, or industry benchmark
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Elevated material costs squeeze margin directly and create urgency for efficiency or substitution innovation.
variables.comment: Same sector-benchmark caveat as Materials Cost below.

variables.label: Innovativeness of product
variables.source_text_sheet: Product catalogs (historical versions via Wayback Machine), press releases, trade fair exhibitor archives

sources: Product catalogs via Wayback (product_catalog_crawler)

variables.proxy: Time since last meaningful product update, from product catalog version history or press mentions
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A product line that hasn't meaningfully changed in years is the textbook target for an innovation pilot.
variables.comment: Best corroborated with Product Age and Patents, a single missing update is not conclusive on its own.

variables.label: Quality of product

applicability.rationale: Row 29 measures quality outcome through customer reviews; B2B industrial firms mostly have none. Row 74 then carries the QUALITY redundancy group alone.

variables.source_text_sheet: Google Reviews, Trustpilot, industry review platforms, first-contact interview for B2B companies with no public reviews

sources: Google Reviews / Trustpilot (review_crawler, gated); B2B usually not applicable

variables.proxy: Review sentiment trend over time on Google/Trustpilot/industry-specific review platforms
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A declining quality trend visible in customer reviews is a direct, externally verifiable pain point a pilot could target.
variables.comment: If review volume is too low to be reliable (typical for B2B manufacturers), fall back on warranty claim rates or complaint data gathered at first contact instead.

variables.label: Type of product
variables.status_text: Physical / manufactured good (example value, see comment)

status_mapping.note: Moderator row: never scored. Named labels exist only so moderators.json rules can match on them; they carry no axis values.

variables.source_text_sheet: Company website, product catalog

sources: Company website / catalog; ATECO code (AIDA) as a cross-check (TO_MAP: header)

variables.proxy: Product category classification (physical good, service, hybrid, B2B component, B2C finished good)
variables.indicator_text: [CONTEXT] This variable does not behave like the others: it is a segmentation filter for matching pilot type to product type (a physical-goods manufacturer needs a different pilot design than a services business), not a need or readiness score.
variables.comment: Flagging structurally: scoring this 'high/low' the way the rest of the table does would not be meaningful. Consider moving it into a separate classification tag rather than the scored table.

variables.label: Product age
variables.source_text_sheet: Company 'our history' page, trade press archives

sources: TO_MAP: 'chi siamo' history page, trade press archives

variables.proxy: Year of original product launch, from company history page or trade press archives
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] An old core product line still generating the bulk of revenue is an obsolescence risk and a clear need signal, especially paired with the Innovativeness of Product and Quality of Product rows.
variables.comment: Overlaps with Innovativeness of Product; consider merging the two if scoring redundancy becomes an issue at implementation.

variables.label: Difficulty of logistics
variables.source_text_sheet: Annual report supply chain notes, first-contact interview, trade press on sector logistics norms

sources: First-contact questionnaire; bilancio supply chain notes

variables.proxy: Number of distribution intermediaries or handling steps between production and end customer, from supply chain disclosures or first-contact interview
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Complex, multi-step logistics is a concrete operational pain point that logistics-tech or route-optimization pilots can directly address.
variables.comment: Mostly relevant to companies with physical distribution; treat as not applicable for pure services or software.

variables.label: EBIT
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'RISULTATO OPERATIVO' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: EBIT trend over the past 3 fiscal years, from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Declining operating profit is the clearest top-level financial pressure signal.
variables.comment: A company under enough financial pressure to show consistently falling EBIT may also lack the discretionary budget to fund even a low-cost pilot; treat a severe or multi-year decline as a distress flag rather than a pure opportunity signal.

variables.label: Gross Margin
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Margine sui consumi' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)
AIDA export header 'Ricavi vendite e prestazioni' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Gross margin trend over the past 3 fiscal years, from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Margin compression signals unresolved cost or pricing pressure that a structured pilot can target.
variables.comment: Compare against sector benchmarks rather than an absolute threshold, margin norms vary widely by industry.

variables.label: Revenues
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Ricavi vendite e prestazioni' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Revenue trend over the past 3 fiscal years, from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Flat or declining top line is a direct growth-pressure signal.
variables.comment: Check whether stagnation is company-specific or an entire-sector pattern (e.g. a shrinking category) before treating it as an internal NEED signal.

variables.label: Interest Coverage Ratio
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings (EBIT and interest expense lines)

sources: AIDA export header 'Grado di copertura degli interessi passivi' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: EBIT ÷ interest expense, computed from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A weakening ability to cover debt service signals financial strain.
variables.comment: Same distress caveat as the EBIT row: a very low ratio indicates distress severe enough to crowd out discretionary pilot budget, don't read the trend alone without checking the absolute level.

variables.label: Materials Cost
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Materie prime e consumo' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Materials cost as % of revenue, trend over 3 years, from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Rising input costs squeeze margin and motivate sourcing or process innovation.
variables.comment: Sensitive to commodity price cycles outside the company's control, corroborate with Cost of Raw Materials before treating as a company-specific signal.

variables.label: Labour Cost
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Totale costi del personale' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Personnel cost as % of revenue, trend over 3 years
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Rising labor cost share increases the appeal of automation or productivity-focused pilots.
variables.comment: Rising labor cost share can also simply reflect a tight regional labor market rather than a company-specific issue, check against Bundesagentur für Arbeit regional wage data.

variables.label: Logistics Costs
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger notes where disclosed, industry logistics cost benchmarks

sources: TO_MAP: nota integrativa 'costi per servizi' detail (trasporti); not a standard AIDA column

variables.proxy: Freight/distribution cost line as % of revenue if disclosed, else industry benchmark
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Rising logistics costs motivate route, warehousing, or fulfillment innovation.
variables.comment: Rarely broken out separately in small-company filings; industry benchmark may be the only available proxy.

variables.label: Energy Costs
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger notes where disclosed, sector energy intensity benchmarks, press coverage of energy cost impact by sector

sources: TO_MAP: nota integrativa 'costi per servizi' / utenze detail; not a standard AIDA column

variables.proxy: Energy cost line as % of revenue if disclosed, else sector energy-intensity benchmark
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Rising energy costs are an especially strong, currently topical pressure point in the German Mittelstand post-2022 energy price shock, motivating efficiency and energy-transition pilots.
variables.comment: Especially relevant for energy-intensive manufacturing; less diagnostic for services businesses.

variables.label: COGS
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Margine sui consumi' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC) (materials-based proxy, see indicator_gaps.GAP_PLAN)

variables.proxy: COGS as % of revenue, trend over 3 years
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] A composite of the cost-pressure rows above; rising COGS share is the aggregate signal.
variables.comment: Largely a rollup of Materials/Labour/Logistics/Energy above; decide whether a scoring model needs both the components and this aggregate, or just one.

variables.label: Service Costs
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA cost breakdown 'Costi per servizi' (aida_cost_breakdown_import.py)

variables.proxy: Purchased services cost line as % of revenue, from Bundesanzeiger notes
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Rising third-party service spend can indicate the company is already outsourcing functions it lacks in-house capability for, a related but distinct NEED signal from raw cost pressure.
variables.comment: Distinguish from Labour Cost: rising service costs point to external outsourcing dependency, not internal headcount cost.

variables.label: R&D Expenses

status_mapping.note: Rows 43/44 [READINESS-GAP / GG-FIT]: the tag contains READINESS and not NEGATIVE, so Standard: low/zero R&D RAISES the READINESS-axis value, as the row text frames it (fit signal for an external pilot).

variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger filings (if R&D costs are broken out), DPMA patent filing history as proxy

sources: Bilancio: capitalised research & development in AIDA intangibles detail (TO_MAP: header); UIBM / EPO patents as proxy

variables.proxy: R&D/development cost line if capitalized or disclosed, else patent filing activity as proxy
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS-GAP / GG-FIT] Low or zero internal R&D spend does not necessarily mean the company perceives no need, it usually means there is no internal alternative to an external pilot. This is less a need signal and more a fit signal for why GG rather than in-house R&D.
variables.comment: Don't read as low ambition, read as low internal capability, which strengthens rather than weakens GG's pitch.

variables.label: Patents

status_mapping.note: Rows 43/44 [READINESS-GAP / GG-FIT]: the tag contains READINESS and not NEGATIVE, so Standard: low/zero R&D RAISES the READINESS-axis value, as the row text frames it (fit signal for an external pilot).

variables.source_text_sheet: DPMA register, EPO Espacenet

sources: EPO OPS adapter (adapters/epo_ops.py)
UIBM patent register (TO_MAP: access)

variables.proxy: Patent filing count and recency, from DPMA (German Patent and Trademark Office) or EPO Espacenet
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS-GAP / GG-FIT] Same logic as R&D Expenses: limited patent activity signals the company hasn't pursued the traditional in-house innovation route, making an external, pilot-based model more relevant rather than less.
variables.comment: Absence of patents is normal and uninformative in many services or trade-oriented Mittelstand sectors; weight this variable down outside of manufacturing/technical sectors.

variables.label: Trademarks
variables.source_text_sheet: DPMA trademark register

sources: EUIPO adapter (adapters/euipo.py)
UIBM trademark register (TO_MAP: access)

variables.proxy: Number of new trademark filings in the past 2-3 years, from the DPMA register
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Active trademark filing suggests the company is bringing new products, sub-brands, or services to market right now, a positive, verifiable signal of present-tense openness rather than stated intent.
variables.comment: A useful complement to the low-patent signal above: together they suggest a company innovating at the brand/go-to-market level but not the technical/product level, exactly where GG-brokered pilots could add the most value.

variables.label: Participations in subsidiaries
variables.source_text_sheet: Handelsregister, Bundesanzeiger consolidated financial statement notes

sources: AIDA STRUCTURE_LEGAL_OWNERSHIP export (partecipazioni)
Registro Imprese

variables.proxy: Number of registered subsidiary/shareholding interests, from Handelsregister/Bundesanzeiger consolidated notes
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] A simple corporate structure with few or no subsidiaries means less internal complexity and bureaucracy to navigate before a pilot decision can be made.
variables.comment: A holding structure with several subsidiaries is common for tax or succession-planning reasons unrelated to complexity; verify at first contact before reading it negatively.

variables.label: CapEx
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'Immobilizzazioni materiali: (Investimenti)' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)
AIDA export header 'Immobilizzazioni immateriali: (Investimenti)' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)
AIDA export header 'Ricavi vendite e prestazioni' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: CapEx as % of revenue, trend over 3 years, from Bundesanzeiger filings
variables.indicator_text: [NEED] Persistently low capital investment signals underinvestment in physical or technological capacity, a stagnation risk.
variables.comment: Low CapEx can also reflect a deliberately conservative, cash-preserving management style that may extend to reluctance in funding a pilot too; verify management's stated investment appetite at first contact rather than assuming low CapEx equals high appetite for a pilot.

variables.label: Total Assets
variables.source_text_sheet: Bundesanzeiger annual filings

sources: AIDA export header 'TOTALE ATTIVO' (aida_import.SERIES_SPEC)

variables.proxy: Total assets from balance sheet, Bundesanzeiger
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] A medium asset base signals enough absorptive infrastructure to actually host and integrate a pilot's output, too small and there's nothing to attach the innovation to, too large and bureaucracy slows everything down.
variables.comment: Should have some absorbtive infrastructure

variables.label: Cash

sources: First-contact questionnaire (primary); Italian job postings naming several systems or integration roles (InfoJobs, Indeed Italia, LinkedIn); DREAMY integration questions as a question bank

variables.proxy: Degree to which planning, production, maintenance, quality and finance data sit in connected systems rather than in spreadsheets and re-keyed exports. Inferred from the number and mix of systems named in job postings, integration or interface roles, and first-contact disclosure.
variables.indicator_text: [NEED, readiness caveat] Siloed systems signal an unmet need for exactly the cross-functional visibility that project performance and governance tools provide. Fully manual reconciliation also predicts that pilot data will be slow and error-prone to collect, so it caps readiness.
variables.comment: Derived from the DREAMY maturity model (De Carolis et al., 2025, IJPR), where integration and interoperability is the step that separates Defined from Integrated companies and a Digital Backbone is treated as a cross-cutting layer. It splits out of row 63, which was mixing two different things: how old a system is and how well it connects to the others. Read the two together but do not average them blindly, because an old but integrated system and a new but siloed one imply different pilots.

variables.label: Quality process maturity
variables.status_text: No recognised certification where the sector norm requires one (or inspector-driven, undocumented quality)

status_mapping.note: Row 74 [BOTH]: ONE observation, TWO mappings. 'No recognised certification where the sector norm requires one' feeds NEED only; 'long held, multi-standard certification' feeds READINESS (and zeroes the NEED gap). null = this state does not contribute to that axis (READINESS coverage is then lower for that company, never scored as bad). The Sheet1 status also names 'inspector-driven, undocumented quality' as a NEED trigger.

variables.source_text_sheet: Accredia (Italian accreditation body) certified organisations data, subject to confirming bulk access; certification body registers (RINA, DNV, TUV, Bureau Veritas); company website quality page; first-contact questionnaire for depth

Certification body registers (RINA, DNV, TUV, Bureau Veritas)
Company website quality page
First-contact questionnaire for depth

variables.proxy: Management system certifications held (ISO 9001, IATF 16949 for automotive, AS9100 for aerospace, ISO 3834 or EN 15085 for welding and rail), their scope and how long they have been held.
variables.indicator_text: [BOTH] Absence of a certification that sector peers hold signals a quality process gap (NEED). A long held, multi-standard certification signals documented processes and an organisation able to define pilot metrics (READINESS). Always read against the sector norm, not in absolute terms.
variables.comment: Complements row 29 (Quality of product), which measures the outcome through customer reviews. DREAMY separates product quality outcome from the maturity of the quality process, and reviews are mostly unavailable for B2B industrial firms, so certification is the more reliable proxy for this ICP. Certification is a floor, not a ceiling: a certified firm can still run paper checklists, so confirm depth at first contact.

variables.label: Prior digital maturity self-assessment
variables.status_text: Completed, low to medium maturity (DREAMY levels 1 to 3)

status_mapping.note: Row 75 [READINESS], asymmetric by design: a completed assessment at DREAMY level 1-3 is a positive READINESS/openness signal. No record is UNKNOWN (interactions.json asymmetric_variables), never low. A completed level 4-5 assessment is not described in the sheet: its value is TO_CALIBRATE and until set the observation is treated as unknown with a warning. Levels 4-5 = assumption (5-level model).

variables.source_text_sheet: Digital Innovation Hub partnership or consent-based data sharing, testindustria4-0.com assessment (self reported), first-contact questionnaire

sources: Digital Innovation Hub partnership / consent-based data sharing (DIH network); testindustria4-0.com self-reported; first-contact questionnaire

variables.proxy: Whether the company has taken a structured digital maturity assessment (Test Your Industry 4.0 / DREAMY via a Digital Innovation Hub, or a comparable audit) and the level obtained.
variables.indicator_text: [READINESS] Having completed an assessment is a strong openness signal, because the company has already looked at its own gaps. A low to medium result in the relevant area is exactly the target profile of high openness with low or medium readiness.
variables.comment: Very high value but low coverage: results are self reported, held by the Hubs, and usable only with consent, so treat it as a partnership or first-contact data point, not a desk research variable. Caveat: DREAMY benchmarks are per sector and built on the 250+ companies that applied, a likely self-selected sample, so a level is only comparable within its sector and may overstate the population.
